name: Dorsal approach for wrist-spanning bridge plate
region: dorsal wrist, distal radius, and third metacarpal
corridor: Third extensor-compartment release with radial EPL transposition and subperiosteal elevation of the intact fourth compartment

positioning.text: Position supine with arm on a radiolucent hand table, forearm pronated, and elbow and shoulder accessible for traction and imaging.

setup.text: Template plate length and metacarpal choice, plan proximal and distal windows and tendon-safe tunnel, and counsel that planned plate removal is usually required.

surface_landmarks.text: Mark Lister tubercle, EPL course, third metacarpal, wrist joint, radial shaft, and superficial radial nerve territory.

incision.text: Use aligned dorsal windows over distal radius and third metacarpal, extending the central exposure as needed for third-compartment release.

superficial_interval.text: Mobilize flaps carefully to protect superficial radial nerve branches and identify extensor compartments before tunneling.

deep_interval.text: Open the third compartment in line with EPL without cutting it, transpose EPL radially, and elevate the intact fourth compartment subperiosteally toward the third metacarpal.

layers.text: Skin, subcutaneous nerve plane, extensor retinaculum, third-compartment sheath, subperiosteal fourth-compartment plane, then radius and third metacarpal.

structures_encountered.text: EPL, EDC/EIP compartment, second compartment when mobilized, dorsal capsule, radius, and third metacarpal are encountered.

structures_at_risk.text: EPL and other extensor tendons, superficial radial nerve, posterior interosseous nerve distally, dorsal sensory branches, and articular surfaces are at risk.

danger_zones.text: Confirm the plate lies deep to tendons without trapping EPL or fourth-compartment tendons and avoid blind passage off bone.

retraction_hazards.text: Use vessel-loop control of EPL without excessive traction and avoid crushing the intact fourth compartment against retractors or plate.

exposure.text: Provides a dorsal internal-fixator corridor from radial shaft across wrist to third metacarpal and can expose the intermediate column.

limitations.text: Temporarily sacrifices wrist motion, usually requires removal, and may not directly reduce all articular fragments without adjunct windows.

extensions.text: Mobilize second compartment radially or extend radius/metacarpal windows for direct plate seating and fragment-specific adjunct fixation.

indications.text: Use for severely comminuted intra-articular fractures, poor distal fixation stock, selected polytrauma load-bearing needs, or wrist fusion.

relative_contraindications.text: Avoid when a nonspanning construct can reliably restore anatomy and motion, or dorsal soft tissue and tendon conditions cannot tolerate the plate.

implant_implications.text: Seat the bridge plate deep to tendons on radius and third metacarpal, restore length by ligamentotaxis without overdistraction, and plan later removal.

fluoroscopy_implications.text: Confirm radial length, inclination, tilt, articular alignment, metacarpal and radial screw length, and absence of overdistraction.

closure.text: Verify tendon glide and plate coverage, leave EPL safely transposed as planned, repair retinacular intervals without constriction, and close in layers.

complications.text: Complications include tendon adhesion or rupture, digital stiffness, hardware failure, infection, nonunion or malunion, pain, and planned reoperation for removal.

bailouts.text: Open an additional window if the plate cannot pass on bone or tendons cannot be protected; add fragment-specific fixation when ligamentotaxis is insufficient.

procedure_applications.condition: A highly comminuted intra-articular fracture needs internal wrist-spanning fixation or the patient requires a durable load-sharing construct
A dorsal spanning exposure is required for wrist fusion

questions.question: Which compartment is opened completely?
questions.answer: The third extensor compartment containing EPL.

questions.question: How is the fourth compartment handled?
questions.answer: It is elevated subperiosteally while kept intact.

questions.question: What major treatment tradeoff should be discussed?
questions.answer: Temporary wrist immobilization and a planned second operation for plate removal.
